text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The paper publishes a document that it says shows former interior minister Mehmet Agar authorised a gun license for a wanted far-right gangster.
- Government MP at centre of scandal speaks to prosecutor.
- Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller prevents the sending of a Turkish representative to a women parliamentarians' conference in Tehran.
- Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan meets interior mimister and Istanbul's police chief over scandal.
- New book says insider trading and manipulation was discovered at 30 companies on the Istanbul stock exchange last year.
- Police teams force liberal Alevi Moslems to flee villages in eastern province for allegedly helping Kurdish rebels.
- Major hazlenut cooperative fails to pay producers for the last 2.5 months.
- National Security Council approved the use of gangsters for political dirty work at a meeting in 1993.
- Erbakan says European Union is trying to keep Turkey out.
